title: Number, Math & BigInt
lede: Number, Math, and the two global parse helpers, backed by IEEE-754 doubles with an exact-i64 fast path where the inputs are integers. The divergences cluster in two spots: the string-rendering methods (toString/toPrecision/toExponential) pad exponents to two digits (`e+05` vs `e+5`) and truncate a fractional receiver before radix rendering, and the parse helpers inherit their C runtime's quirks — no hex auto-detect for parseInt, and strtod extras like `"inf"` for parseFloat. Everything else — the constants, the trig/log/hyperbolic family, and the bit ops — matches real JS.

entries.name: Number.isInteger(x)
entries.description: Reports whether x is a finite integer value. Checks floor(x) == x on the double.
differences: `Number.isInteger(Infinity)`/`(-Infinity)` return `true` — should be `false`; `emitNumberIsInteger` checks `floor(x) == x` only, never finiteness, and `floor(Infinity) == Infinity` is trivially true.

entries.name: Number.isFinite(x)
entries.description: True when x is a finite number (not NaN, not ±Infinity). Unlike the global isFinite, does not coerce non-number arguments.

entries.name: Number.isNaN(x)
entries.description: True only when x is the NaN value itself — the non-coercing sibling of the global isNaN.

entries.name: Number.isSafeInteger(x)
entries.description: True when x is an integer that round-trips exactly through a double — i.e. within ±(2^53 − 1).

entries.name: Number.parseInt(s)
entries.description: Parses a leading integer out of s. Returns a double (as real JS), so a no-digits input is a real NaN via an endptr-checked strtoll.
differences: No hex auto-detect when radix is omitted — `"0x1F"` parses as `0`, not `31`.

entries.name: Number.parseFloat(s)
entries.description: Parses a leading floating-point number out of s. A no-conversion input returns a real NaN via the endptr check.
differences: Inherits `strtod` extras — `"inf"` parses to `Infinity` (JS only accepts the full word `Infinity`) and C hex-float syntax parses.

entries.name: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
entries.description: The largest integer that round-trips through a double, 2^53 − 1 (9007199254740991).

entries.name: Number.MIN_SAFE_INTEGER
entries.description: The most-negative safe integer, −(2^53 − 1).

entries.name: Number.EPSILON
entries.description: The difference between 1 and the smallest double greater than 1, 2^-52.

entries.name: Number.MAX_VALUE
entries.description: The largest representable positive double, roughly 1.7976931348623157e+308.

entries.name: Number.MIN_VALUE
entries.description: The smallest representable positive (subnormal) double, roughly 5e-324.

entries.name: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY
entries.description: The +Infinity value.

entries.name: Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY
entries.description: The −Infinity value.

entries.name: Number.NaN
entries.description: The NaN value, as a Number static property.

entries.name: Number.prototype.toFixed(n)
entries.description: Formats x with a fixed number of digits after the decimal point.
differences: The `digits` argument is required here, not optional — `(3.14159).toFixed()` hard compile-errors with "toFixed takes exactly 1 argument"; real JS defaults `digits` to `0`.

entries.name: Number.prototype.toString(radix?)
entries.description: Renders x as a string, optionally in a given radix via a hand-rolled digit loop.
differences: Truncates a non-integer receiver to its integer part first (real JS renders fractional digits).
Radix trusted, not validated (real JS throws a `RangeError` for an out-of-range radix).
Minor cosmetic deviations from real JS, the same `sprintf`-based exponent padding as the two rows below.

entries.name: Number.prototype.toPrecision(n)
entries.description: Formats x to the given number of significant digits via sprintf("%#.*g", ...).
differences: Exponent pads to 2 digits — `e+05` vs real JS's `e+5`.

entries.name: Number.prototype.toExponential(n)
entries.description: Formats x in exponential notation with the given fraction digits via sprintf("%.*e", ...).

entries.name: parseInt(s, radix?) (global)
entries.description: The global parseInt — same runtime as Number.parseInt. A no-digits input yields a real NaN.
differences: Same residual as `Number.parseInt(s)` above — no hex auto-detect when radix is omitted.

entries.name: parseFloat(s) (global)
entries.description: The global parseFloat — same runtime as Number.parseFloat. A no-conversion input yields a real NaN.

entries.name: isNaN(x) (global)
entries.description: The global isNaN — true when x is NaN.

entries.name: isFinite(x) (global)
entries.description: The global isFinite — true when x is finite.

entries.name: Math.floor/ceil/round/trunc
entries.description: The four rounding modes. A float input stays a double end-to-end, so NaN/±Infinity pass through unchanged; Math.round uses JS's tie-toward-+Infinity (Math.round(-4.5) === -4), including the -0 result for Math.round(-0.5). An integer input keeps the exact-i64 path.

entries.name: Math.abs
entries.description: Absolute value, preserving the integer fast path for integer inputs.

entries.name: Math.sqrt/pow/hypot
entries.description: Square root, exponentiation, and the Euclidean-norm helper.

entries.name: Math.log/log2/log10
entries.description: Natural, base-2, and base-10 logarithms.

entries.name: Math.sin/cos/tan
entries.description: The primary trigonometric functions (radians).

entries.name: Math.min/max
entries.signature: Math.min(...xs: number[]): number; Math.max(...xs: number[]): number
entries.description: Any float argument promotes the fold to llvm.minimum/llvm.maximum — NaN propagates and -0.0 orders below +0.0, as the JS spec; all-integer calls stay exact i64.

entries.name: Math.sign
entries.description: The float path returns ±1.0 or the input itself (NaN stays NaN, a signed zero keeps its sign); the integer path stays exact i64.

entries.name: Math.random()
entries.description: Returns a float in [0, 1).

entries.name: Math.PI/E/LN2/LN10/SQRT2/LOG2E/LOG10E
entries.signature: Math.PI; Math.E; Math.LN2; Math.LN10; Math.SQRT2; Math.LOG2E; Math.LOG10E
entries.description: The standard Math constants.

entries.name: Math.cbrt/expm1/log1p
entries.description: cbrt uses a deterministic, correctly-rounded fdlibm implementation (@__kml_cbrt) rather than platform libm, whose runtime cbrt is not reliably correctly-rounded and diverged by OS (glibc cbrt(27) gave 3.0000000000000004); expm1/log1p delegate to libm.

entries.name: Math.asin/acos/atan/atan2
entries.description: The inverse trigonometric functions.

entries.name: Math.sinh/cosh/tanh
entries.description: The hyperbolic functions.

entries.name: Math.clz32/fround/imul
entries.description: clz32 via LLVM's own llvm.ctlz.i32 intrinsic; fround via an fptrunc/fpext float32 round-trip; imul via 32-bit mul + sign-extend, giving real 32-bit-wraparound integer multiplication distinct from plain *'s double-precision result.
